primary_source.location: Study title and linked Dryad record
primary_source.finding: The primary study estimates fitness consequences of mutation accumulation across multiple Chlamydomonas strains; the official record links two separately identified fitness-assay blocks.

official_data.finding: The official inventory lists first and second fitness-assay workbooks with distinct checksums and generation data.

records.named_gap: Whether the reported among-strain fitness-effect inference remains stable when estimation is separated across the two documented assay blocks is not resolved by the inventory-level evidence.

outcomes.positive: Agreement across separately estimated blocks would support a bounded claim that the reported strain contrast is not solely assay-block dependent.
outcomes.null: An attenuated or unresolved contrast would restrict the claim to the combined-assay estimate.
outcomes.contrary: A reversed block-separated ordering would change interpretation of the reported strain comparison.

primary_source.finding: The study manipulated bait access at 40 sites and reports that bush-rat visits and foraging declined with possum visits.

official_data.finding: The official inventory lists site-by-night camera-visit events, site covariates, and an analysis notebook.

records.named_gap: The proposed separation of a restricted-access treatment effect from same-night observed possum visits would restate the primary study's manipulated-access and visit-pattern analysis rather than identify a distinct consequence from inventory evidence.

outcomes.positive: Re-estimating the reported access and visit associations would confirm the published foraging result.
outcomes.null: A null reanalysis would not distinguish a new biological consequence from model choice.
outcomes.contrary: A contrary estimate would require primary-paper and causal-role review before it could alter the published interpretation.

primary_source.finding: The experiment manipulated climate and habitat connectivity for three years; population models reset time to zero after extinction and interpret connectivity as altering warming consequences.

official_data.finding: The official inventory lists population-dynamics tables and the corresponding analysis notebook with source-issued digests.

records.named_gap: The effect of resetting time after a population extinction on the bounded climate-by-connectivity population interpretation is not resolved by the stated residual-autocorrelation check.

outcomes.positive: Robustness to calendar-time and post-reinitialization encodings would support the bounded connectivity interpretation.
outcomes.null: Loss of precision or no stable interaction would limit the reported population-dynamics claim.
outcomes.contrary: A material change in the interaction would alter how extinction and recovery contribute to the published conclusion.

next_permitted_action: Retain the one early rejection; complete primary-paper, raw-file, and closest-prior audits for the two eligible records, and source a third record rather than promoting either one.
